title: 人工智能，从零搭建 · 第2部分：有含义的向量

chapters.SVD: 5. 任何矩阵：旋转、拉伸、再旋转
chapters.Outro: 回顾，以及这些想法会在哪里再现

c4798ae0ecec.en: In part one, a model learned to guess the next letter by counting, and it hit a wall. Every context was its own island. <bookmark mark='a'/> Reading the dog barked a hundred times taught it nothing about the hound barked.
c4798ae0ecec.zh: 在第1部分，一个模型靠计数学会了猜下一个字母，然后撞上了一堵墙：每个上下文都是一座孤岛。<bookmark mark='a'/>把the dog barked读上100遍，也没让它学到关于the hound barked的任何东西。

86124b2efa72.en: Every modern model fixes this the same way. It gives each word a place, <bookmark mark='a'/> a point in a space, chosen so that words used alike end up close together. <bookmark mark='b'/> Here are a hundred and two words, where GPT-2 puts them: animals in one region, colors in another, then numbers, places, family, the body, and verbs.
86124b2efa72.zh: 每一个现代模型，都用同一种办法解决这个问题：给每个词一个位置，<bookmark mark='a'/>也就是空间里的一个点，这些点的选法，让用法相近的词最后靠在一起。<bookmark mark='b'/>这是102个词，放在GPT-2给它们安排的位置上：动物在一个区域，颜色在另一个区域，然后是数字、地点、家庭、身体，还有动词。

30a10f3cad30.en: The picture is a shadow. <bookmark mark='a'/> GPT-2 really gives each of its 50,257 tokens a list of 768 numbers, and we've flattened them down to three, keeping the three directions along which these words spread out the most. <bookmark mark='b'/> Up close, dog sits with the other animals.
30a10f3cad30.zh: 这幅图只是一个影子。<bookmark mark='a'/>GPT-2实际上给它的50257个词元，每个都配了一串768个数，我们把它们压扁成3个，留下的是这些词散得最开的3个方向。<bookmark mark='b'/>凑近看，dog和其他动物待在一起。

88068416a280.en: Here is dog, all 768 numbers. <bookmark mark='a'/> Here is puppy. <bookmark mark='b'/> And here is tobacco. <bookmark mark='c'/> Two of these belong together, and in chapter two we'll learn to measure how much.
88068416a280.zh: 这是dog，全部768个数。<bookmark mark='a'/>这是puppy。<bookmark mark='b'/>这是tobacco。<bookmark mark='c'/>其中有两个是一路的，到第2章，我们会学会衡量它们有多接近。

47f913142a43.en: Lists of numbers are vectors, and this part is about what they can do. <bookmark mark='a'/> Measure how alike two things are. Transform a whole space at once. Find the directions that matter most. And live in hundreds of dimensions, where our three-dimensional intuition fails, in useful ways.
47f913142a43.zh: 一串数就是一个向量，这一部分讲的，就是向量能做什么。<bookmark mark='a'/>衡量两样东西有多相似。一下子变换整个空间。找出最要紧的方向。还有，在几百维的空间里生活：在那里，我们三维的直觉会失灵，而且失灵得很有用。

248df66bb3b7.en: A vector is an arrow from the origin, <bookmark mark='a'/> or, just as well, a list of numbers: how far to go along each axis. <bookmark mark='b'/> Two numbers in the plane, three in space, and 768 in GPT-2.
248df66bb3b7.zh: 向量是一根从原点出发的箭头，<bookmark mark='a'/>也同样可以看成一串数：沿每条坐标轴各走多远。<bookmark mark='b'/>平面上是2个数，空间里是3个，GPT-2里是768个。

cc4951481fd4.en: Two moves make all of linear algebra. <bookmark mark='a'/> Add two vectors: walk along one, then along the other. <bookmark mark='b'/> And scale a vector: stretch it, shrink it, or flip it around.
cc4951481fd4.zh: 整个线性代数，只靠两个动作。<bookmark mark='a'/>把两个向量相加：先沿着一个走，再沿着另一个走。<bookmark mark='b'/>还有缩放一个向量：把它拉长、缩短，或者调转方向。

f4b8c70fdfa7.en: Mix the two moves: a times u, plus b times v. <bookmark mark='a'/> As a and b vary, the tip sweeps out the whole plane. <bookmark mark='b'/> u and v are then a basis: every vector has exactly one pair of coordinates in it. The usual axes are just the most familiar basis.
f4b8c70fdfa7.zh: 把两个动作混在一起：a乘u，加上b乘v。<bookmark mark='a'/>a和b一变，箭头的尖端就扫过整个平面。<bookmark mark='b'/>这时u和v就是一组基：每个向量在这组基里，都有唯一的一对坐标。平常的坐标轴，只不过是我们最熟悉的一组基。

7ed1c3eeec5d.en: Chapter two. How alike are two vectors?
7ed1c3eeec5d.zh: 第2章。两个向量有多相似？

c7e6100bc92f.en: How alike are two vectors? <bookmark mark='a'/> Multiply them coordinate by coordinate, and add it all up. That's the dot product. <bookmark mark='b'/> It has a second meaning: the length of one, times the length of the other, times the cosine of the angle between them.
c7e6100bc92f.zh: 两个向量有多相似？<bookmark mark='a'/>把它们一个坐标一个坐标地相乘，再全部加起来。这就是点积。<bookmark mark='b'/>它还有第二层含义：一个的长度，乘以另一个的长度，再乘以它们夹角的余弦。

869bec6cce5d.en: Watch it as one vector turns. <bookmark mark='a'/> Pointing the same way, the dot product is as big as it can get. <bookmark mark='b'/> At a right angle, it's zero. <bookmark mark='c'/> Pointing apart, it's negative. Against a vector of length one, the dot product is the length of the shadow that one vector casts on the other.
869bec6cce5d.zh: 让其中一个向量转起来，看看会怎样。<bookmark mark='a'/>指向同一个方向时，点积最大。<bookmark mark='b'/>成直角时，点积是0。<bookmark mark='c'/>方向相背时，点积是负的。和一个长度为1的向量做点积，得到的就是另一个向量投在它上面的影子的长度。

e1d25c8abe56.en: Divide by the two lengths and you get the cosine similarity, which runs from minus one to one. <bookmark mark='a'/> For GPT-2's words: dog and puppy, 0.62. Dog and cat, 0.55. Dog and tobacco, 0.23. <bookmark mark='b'/> In 768 dimensions you can't draw the angle, but you can compute it: multiply the two lists number by number, and add.
e1d25c8abe56.zh: 再除以两个长度，就得到余弦相似度，它的取值从负1到1。<bookmark mark='a'/>拿GPT-2的词来算：dog和puppy是0.62，dog和cat是0.55，dog和tobacco是0.23。<bookmark mark='b'/>在768维里，夹角画不出来，但可以算出来：把两串数逐个相乘，再加起来。

c8363f94105e.en: Here is why this matters. In part one, a network ended with a score for every possible next token, and the softmax turned the scores into probabilities. <bookmark mark='a'/> In GPT-2, every one of those scores is a dot product: the model's final state, dotted with each token's vector, the very same vectors the tokens started out as. <bookmark mark='b'/> After the Eiffel Tower is located in the city of, the biggest dot product belongs to Paris, then London, then Amsterdam. <bookmark mark='c'/> Only the differences matter: the softmax gives Paris 6.4 percent, the number we met in part one.
c8363f94105e.zh: 这件事为什么要紧？在第1部分，网络最后会给每一个可能的下一个词元打一个分，再由softmax把分数变成概率。<bookmark mark='a'/>在GPT-2里，每一个分数都是一个点积：模型的最终状态，与每个词元的向量做点积，而这些向量，正是词元一开始的那些向量。<bookmark mark='b'/>在“埃菲尔铁塔所在的城市是”这半句话后面，点积最大的是巴黎，然后是伦敦，再然后是阿姆斯特丹。<bookmark mark='c'/>要紧的只是差值：softmax给巴黎6.4%，就是我们在第1部分见过的那个数。

f820be8e45a9.en: A matrix moves every vector at once. <bookmark mark='a'/> It keeps the origin where it is, and keeps grid lines straight, parallel, and evenly spaced: it's a linear map. <bookmark mark='b'/> Watch the whole plane move.
f820be8e45a9.zh: 矩阵一下子移动所有的向量。<bookmark mark='a'/>它让原点保持不动，让网格线保持笔直、平行、间距均匀：这就是线性映射。<bookmark mark='b'/>看整个平面动起来。

2c0a5eaeeeff.en: Where does each vector go? <bookmark mark='a'/> Only two arrows decide it: where the two basis arrows land. Those landing spots are the columns of the matrix. <bookmark mark='b'/> A vector with coordinates one and two lands at one times the first column, plus two times the second. That's what multiplying a matrix by a vector means.
2c0a5eaeeeff.zh: 每个向量会被送到哪里？<bookmark mark='a'/>只由两根箭头决定：两根基向量箭头落在哪里。这两个落点，就是矩阵的两列。<bookmark mark='b'/>坐标为1和2的向量，会落在1乘第一列、加上2乘第二列的地方。矩阵乘以向量，说的就是这个。

11dafb04efc9.en: One map after another is again a map, and its matrix is the product of the two. <bookmark mark='a'/> But the order matters: turning, then shearing, is not shearing, then turning.
11dafb04efc9.zh: 一个映射接着另一个映射，仍然是一个映射，它的矩阵就是两个矩阵的乘积。<bookmark mark='a'/>但顺序很要紧：先旋转再错切，和先错切再旋转，是不一样的。

d4c62614bc14.en: One number says how much a map stretches area: the determinant. <bookmark mark='a'/> The unit square becomes a parallelogram, and the determinant is its area. <bookmark mark='b'/> When the determinant reaches zero, the whole plane is squashed onto a line, and information is lost for good. <bookmark mark='c'/> Below zero, the plane has been flipped over, like a page turned face down.
d4c62614bc14.zh: 有一个数，能说明映射把面积拉伸了多少：行列式。<bookmark mark='a'/>单位正方形变成一个平行四边形，行列式就是它的面积。<bookmark mark='b'/>行列式一旦变成0，整个平面就被压扁到一条线上，信息就永远丢失了。<bookmark mark='c'/>小于0时，平面被翻了过来，就像一页纸被扣过去，正面朝下。

8bb7aff8e10a.en: Most vectors are knocked off their line by a matrix. <bookmark mark='a'/> But some aren't: they stay on their own line, and are only stretched or shrunk. <bookmark mark='b'/> Those are the eigenvectors, and the stretch factor is the eigenvalue.
8bb7aff8e10a.zh: 大多数向量，都会被矩阵撞离它原来所在的那条直线。<bookmark mark='a'/>但有些不会：它们留在自己的直线上，只被拉长或缩短。<bookmark mark='b'/>这些就是特征向量，拉伸的倍数就是特征值。

7d3a6914d4ad.en: Symmetric matrices, the ones that equal their own mirror image across the diagonal, behave best of all. <bookmark mark='a'/> Their eigenvalues are real numbers, and their eigenvectors are perpendicular. <bookmark mark='b'/> So the map is: turn, so the eigenvectors line up with the axes; stretch along each axis by its eigenvalue; and turn back. <bookmark mark='c'/> A equals Q, Lambda, Q transpose. That's the spectral theorem.
7d3a6914d4ad.zh: 对称矩阵，也就是沿对角线翻过来和自己一模一样的矩阵，性质最好。<bookmark mark='a'/>它们的特征值都是实数，特征向量互相垂直。<bookmark mark='b'/>所以这个映射就是：先旋转，让特征向量对准坐标轴；再沿每条轴，按各自的特征值拉伸；最后转回去。<bookmark mark='c'/>A等于Q、Λ、Q转置。这就是谱定理。

2912912b833d.en: Covariance matrices, which describe how data spreads out, are symmetric, and their eigenvectors point along the directions in which the data spreads the most. <bookmark mark='a'/> These are the principal components. <bookmark mark='b'/> Keeping only the top few, and dropping the rest, is how we drew GPT-2's 768-dimensional words in three dimensions at the start of this part.
2912912b833d.zh: 协方差矩阵描述数据是怎样散开的，它是对称的，它的特征向量指向数据散得最开的那些方向。<bookmark mark='a'/>这些就是主成分。<bookmark mark='b'/>只留下最靠前的几个，其余的丢掉：这一部分开头，我们就是这样把GPT-2的768维的词画到三维里的。

dbc7ad85bef6.en: Chapter five. The singular value decomposition.

bad90ada8f0d.en: Not every matrix is symmetric. Many aren't even square. <bookmark mark='a'/> But every matrix, without exception, does three things: a turn, then a stretch along the axes, then another turn. <bookmark mark='b'/> That's the singular value decomposition: A equals U, Sigma, V transpose.
bad90ada8f0d.zh: 不是每个矩阵都是对称的。很多甚至都不是方阵。<bookmark mark='a'/>但每一个矩阵，无一例外，都只做三件事：一次旋转，然后沿坐标轴拉伸，然后再一次旋转。<bookmark mark='b'/>这就是奇异值分解：A等于U、Σ、V转置。

d233554528e2.en: The stretches are the singular values. <bookmark mark='a'/> The unit circle always becomes an ellipse, and the singular values are its half-axes. <bookmark mark='b'/> Sweep a unit vector all the way around, and watch how long its image is. The longest it ever gets is sigma one: the most the matrix can stretch any vector. It's called the spectral norm.
d233554528e2.zh: 这些拉伸的倍数就是奇异值。<bookmark mark='a'/>单位圆总会变成一个椭圆，奇异值就是它的半轴长。<bookmark mark='b'/>让一个单位向量转上一整圈，看它的像有多长。最长的时候是σ1：也就是这个矩阵能把任何向量拉伸的最大倍数。它叫作谱范数。

84014fdcae09.en: Why care how much a matrix stretches? <bookmark mark='a'/> A deep network applies one matrix after another. Push a vector through forty layers of random matrices. <bookmark mark='b'/> If each layer stretches a typical vector by 1.2, after forty layers its length has grown two thousand times. <bookmark mark='c'/> At 0.8, it shrinks to almost nothing. Only near one does the signal survive. That knife edge is the subject of part eight.
84014fdcae09.zh: 为什么要关心矩阵拉伸多少？<bookmark mark='a'/>深度网络就是一个矩阵接着一个矩阵地作用。让一个向量穿过40层随机矩阵。<bookmark mark='b'/>如果每一层都把一个典型的向量拉长到1.2倍，40层之后，它的长度会变成原来的大约2000倍。<bookmark mark='c'/>如果是0.8，它就缩到几乎没有了。只有在1附近，信号才能活下来。这道刀锋，就是第8部分的主题。

5126432ab535.en: There's more. Written out, the decomposition says that any matrix is a sum of simple pieces, <bookmark mark='a'/> each one a column times a row, weighted by a singular value. <bookmark mark='b'/> Keep the k biggest pieces, drop the rest, and you get the closest possible matrix built from only k pieces. No other choice comes closer. That's the Eckart–Young theorem, from 1936.
5126432ab535.zh: 还不止这些。把这个分解展开来写，它说的是：任何矩阵都是一些简单小块之和，<bookmark mark='a'/>每一块都是一列乘以一行，再以一个奇异值作为权重。<bookmark mark='b'/>留下最大的k块，丢掉其余的，就得到只用k块拼成的、最接近原矩阵的矩阵。没有别的选法能更接近。这就是埃卡特–扬定理，1936年提出。

6f5416e0575d.en: Here's a real matrix: part one's table of letter pairs, twenty-six letters by twenty-six. <bookmark mark='a'/> The first piece alone already has the broad shape: it's the table you'd get if the next letter didn't care what came before. <bookmark mark='b'/> Add the second piece, the third, the fifth, the tenth, <bookmark mark='c'/> and the error falls by exactly the singular values left out: 0.56 of the whole after one piece, 0.40 after two.
6f5416e0575d.zh: 来看一个真实的矩阵：第1部分的字母对表，26个字母乘26个字母。<bookmark mark='a'/>光是第一块，就已经有了大致的轮廓：如果下一个字母根本不在乎前面是什么，得到的就是这张表。<bookmark mark='b'/>加上第二块、第三块、第五块、第十块，<bookmark mark='c'/>误差随之下降，剩下多少，恰好由被丢掉的那些奇异值决定：只留一块时，是整体的0.56，留两块时，是0.40。

560e2c5eea31.en: The pieces mean something, too. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take the way the table departs from independence, and spread the letters out along its strongest direction. <bookmark mark='b'/> At one end: i, a, o, u, e. No one told the computer what a vowel is. From counts alone, it found that vowels and consonants take turns.
560e2c5eea31.zh: 这些小块也有含义。<bookmark mark='a'/>取出这张表偏离独立性的那部分，把字母沿着它最强的方向排开。<bookmark mark='b'/>一端是：i、a、o、u、e。没有人告诉计算机什么是元音。光凭计数，它就发现了元音和辅音是轮流出现的。

3e6344567185.en: Now the same, with words. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take the ten thousand most common words in the thirty books, and count how often each pair turns up within four words of each other: a table with a hundred million cells, from four point three five million words of text. <bookmark mark='b'/> Then turn the counts into surprise, part one's way: how much more often do two words meet than they would by chance? That's the pointwise mutual information. Keep its positive part.
3e6344567185.zh: 现在对词做同样的事。<bookmark mark='a'/>取那30本书里最常见的1万个词，数一数每一对词在彼此相距4个词以内出现了多少次：这是一张有1亿个格子的表，来自435万个词的文本。<bookmark mark='b'/>然后按第1部分的办法，把计数变成意外度：两个词相遇的次数，比纯属偶然时多出多少？这就是逐点互信息。只保留它的正值部分。

ac845b981fe0.en: Then keep the table's hundred strongest directions, with the singular value decomposition. <bookmark mark='a'/> Every word gets a hundred numbers. <bookmark mark='b'/> And words that keep the same company end up close together. Monday: Saturday, Tuesday, Sunday. Three: four, two, five. Dog: dogs, sheep, wolf, cat, and Perezvon, which, in The Brothers Karamazov, is a dog. Nobody gave it a dictionary.
ac845b981fe0.zh: 接着用奇异值分解，只留下这张表里最强的100个方向。<bookmark mark='a'/>这样，每个词就都有了自己的100个数。<bookmark mark='b'/>和同一批词做伴的词，最后会彼此靠得很近。离monday最近的，是saturday、tuesday和sunday。离three最近的，是four、two和five。离dog最近的，则是dogs、sheep、wolf和cat，最后还有perezvon：在《卡拉马佐夫兄弟》里，它是一条狗。从来没有人给过它一本词典。

af1338f0dda0.en: Directions mean something too. <bookmark mark='a'/> Start at France, and step to Paris. Then take the same step, starting from England. <bookmark mark='b'/> The nearest word to where you land is London. Man is to king as woman is to: duke first, then queen. Novels from the nineteenth century had their own ideas.
af1338f0dda0.zh: 方向也有含义。<bookmark mark='a'/>从france出发，走到paris。再从england出发，迈出同样的一步。<bookmark mark='b'/>离落脚点最近的词，是london。man之于king，正如woman之于什么？排第一的是duke，公爵；然后才是queen，女王。19世纪的小说，自有它们的想法。

213ccb730862.en: In 2013, Tomas Mikolov and his colleagues at Google trained word vectors another way: with a guessing game. From each word, guess the words around it. <bookmark mark='a'/> That's word2vec. We trained it on the same books, for three passes. <bookmark mark='b'/> For common words, its neighbours agree with the counting method's. <bookmark mark='c'/> And in 2014, Omer Levy and Yoav Goldberg showed why: word2vec is quietly factorizing the very same table of mutual information. Guessing and counting meet again.
213ccb730862.zh: 2013年，托马斯·米科洛夫和他在谷歌的同事，用另一种办法训练词向量：一个猜词游戏。从每个词出发，猜它周围的词。<bookmark mark='a'/>这就是word2vec。我们在同样的书上训练了它，过了3遍。<bookmark mark='b'/>对常见的词，它找到的近邻，和计数方法找到的一致。<bookmark mark='c'/>2014年，奥默·列维与约阿夫·戈德堡说明了原因：word2vec其实是在悄悄分解同一张互信息表。猜测和计数，又一次相遇了。

54c4910e5cc0.en: Chapter eight. Life in seven hundred and sixty-eight dimensions.

f9731e3614a2.en: Our intuition comes from three dimensions, and in seven hundred and sixty-eight it misleads us. <bookmark mark='a'/> Pick two directions at random. In two dimensions, the angle between them could be anything. <bookmark mark='b'/> In three, angles near a right angle are already the most common. <bookmark mark='c'/> In a hundred, it's almost always within ten degrees of one, <bookmark mark='d'/> and in 768, within about four.
f9731e3614a2.zh: 我们的直觉来自三维，到了768维，它会误导我们。<bookmark mark='a'/>随机取两个方向。在二维里，它们的夹角可以是任何值。<bookmark mark='b'/>在三维里，接近直角的夹角已经是最常见的了。<bookmark mark='c'/>在100维里，夹角几乎总是和直角相差不到10度，<bookmark mark='d'/>而在768维里，相差大约不到4度。

9128d53a5a36.en: So a high-dimensional space is full of room. <bookmark mark='a'/> Ten thousand random directions in 768 dimensions: every pair of them lies between seventy-nine and a hundred and one degrees apart. <bookmark mark='b'/> A model can keep far more features than it has dimensions, as long as they only need to be nearly perpendicular. That idea, superposition, is how we'll read the inside of a model in part twenty.
9128d53a5a36.zh: 所以，高维空间里有的是地方。<bookmark mark='a'/>768维里的1万个随机方向：任意两个之间的夹角，都在79度到101度之间。<bookmark mark='b'/>模型能存下的特征，可以远远多于它的维数，只要这些特征彼此只需近似垂直。这个想法叫叠加，到第20部分，我们就靠它来读懂模型的内部。

b08dc1b99bcb.en: Lengths behave strangely too. <bookmark mark='a'/> Give a vector 768 independent random coordinates, and its length is almost exactly the square root of 768, every time. The spread all but disappears. <bookmark mark='b'/> And nearly all of a ball's volume sits in a thin shell at its surface: in 768 dimensions, 99.96 percent of it lies within one percent of the edge.
b08dc1b99bcb.zh: 长度的表现也很奇怪。<bookmark mark='a'/>给一个向量768个独立的随机坐标，它的长度每次都几乎恰好是根号768。波动几乎完全消失了。<bookmark mark='b'/>而且一个球的体积，几乎全都集中在表面的一层薄壳里：在768维里，99.96%的体积，都在离边界1%的范围之内。

11ca9552ffd0.en: Real word vectors aren't random, though. <bookmark mark='a'/> GPT-2's vectors all lean the same way: two unrelated words have a cosine of 0.24 on average, not zero. <bookmark mark='b'/> Subtract the average vector from every word, and the cosines fall back around zero.
11ca9552ffd0.zh: 不过，真实的词向量并不是随机的。<bookmark mark='a'/>GPT-2的向量都朝同一个方向倾斜：两个不相关的词，余弦平均是0.24，而不是0。<bookmark mark='b'/>从每个词里减去平均向量，余弦就回落到0附近。

d4527e618f2d.en: Here's a consequence that sounds impossible. <bookmark mark='a'/> Take a thousand of GPT-2's vectors, and multiply them all by the same random matrix, crushing 768 numbers down to a few. <bookmark mark='b'/> Down to two, distances are scrambled. Five, twenty: better. <bookmark mark='c'/> At a hundred, 84 percent of the distances move by less than ten percent, and at four hundred, almost all of them.
d4527e618f2d.zh: 有一个推论，听起来简直不可能。<bookmark mark='a'/>取GPT-2的1000个向量，全都乘以同一个随机矩阵，把768个数压到只剩几个。<bookmark mark='b'/>压到2个，距离全乱了。5个、20个：好一些。<bookmark mark='c'/>到100个时，84%的距离变化不到10%，到400个时，几乎全部都是这样。

a10df273923a.en: That's the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma, from 1984. <bookmark mark='a'/> To keep the distances among n points within a factor of one plus or minus epsilon, a random projection to about the log of n over epsilon squared dimensions is enough, whatever dimension you started from. <bookmark mark='b'/> The guarantee is cautious: for our thousand points it asks for five and a half thousand, and four hundred already did the job. <bookmark mark='c'/> The reason it works is the concentration we just saw: a random projection of a vector has nearly the same length, every time.
a10df273923a.zh: 这就是约翰逊–林登施特劳斯引理，1984年提出。<bookmark mark='a'/>要让n个点之间的距离，都保持在1加减ε倍的范围内，只要随机投影到大约n的对数除以ε的平方那么多维就够了，不管一开始是多少维。<bookmark mark='b'/>这个保证很保守：对我们这1000个点，它要求5500维，而400维就已经做到了。<bookmark mark='c'/>它之所以管用，靠的正是我们刚才看到的集中现象：一个向量的随机投影，每次的长度都几乎一样。

a3ee7f23966c.en: Let's take stock. Vectors are arrows, and lists of numbers, and they add and stretch. The dot product measures how alike two of them are, and it's the score behind every next-token guess. Matrices move the whole space at once. Symmetric ones just stretch along perpendicular directions, and every matrix is a turn, a stretch, and a turn. Keeping the biggest pieces of that decomposition found the vowels in letters, and the meanings of words in thirty novels. And in hundreds of dimensions there is room to spare.
a3ee7f23966c.zh: 我们来盘点一下。向量是箭头，也是一串数，它们可以相加，也可以伸缩。点积衡量两个向量有多相似，也是每一次猜下一个词元背后的那个分数。矩阵一下子移动整个空间。对称矩阵只是沿着互相垂直的方向拉伸，而每一个矩阵，都是一次旋转、一次拉伸、再一次旋转。留下这个分解里最大的那几块，就从字母里找出了元音，从30部小说里找出了词的含义。而在几百维的空间里，地方绰绰有余。

517ff53f0462.en: All of it comes back. Attention, the heart of the transformer, is dot products between vectors. A network is matrices, layer after layer, and keeping their stretch near one is how deep networks train at all; one of the newest optimizers works directly on the spectral norm. Low-rank pieces compress the memory of today's largest models. And the room in high dimensions is where models keep more ideas than they have numbers.
517ff53f0462.zh: 这些都会再次出现。注意力是Transformer的核心，它就是向量之间的点积。网络就是一层又一层的矩阵，让它们的拉伸保持在1附近，深度网络才训练得起来；最新的优化器里，就有一个直接作用在谱范数上。低秩的小块，压缩了当今最大模型的记忆。而高维空间里富余的地方，让模型能存下比它拥有的数还要多的想法。

4bcf104452a2.en: Next time: change. Everything in this part stood still. Training moves: every one of a model's numbers is nudged, again and again, in the direction that lowers the loss. <bookmark mark='a'/> Finding that direction for billions of numbers at once is the chain rule, run backwards. Part three builds that machine from scratch.
4bcf104452a2.zh: 下一次：变化。这一部分里的一切都是静止的。训练却在动：模型的每一个数，都被一次又一次地，朝着让损失下降的方向推一点。<bookmark mark='a'/>为几十亿个数同时找到这个方向，靠的是倒过来运行的链式法则。第3部分会从零搭建这台机器。

a9b13cb1d673.en: For more, Gilbert Strang's Linear Algebra and Learning from Data is a friendly companion, and Roman Vershynin's High-Dimensional Probability explains why big spaces behave the way they do. The papers are on screen. Thanks for watching, and see you in part three.
a9b13cb1d673.zh: 想了解更多，吉尔伯特·斯特朗的《线性代数与数据学习》是一本亲切的读物，罗曼·韦尔希宁的《高维概率》则解释了大空间为什么会有这样的表现。论文都列在屏幕上。感谢观看，第3部分见。
